🌍 Iran, China, Russia set conditions for resumption of IAEA verification activities

📌 London, IRNA – Iran, China and Russia say that a complete end to hostile acts, the removal of military threats and credible guarantees against further attacks are prerequisites for the full resumption of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) verification activities in Iran.

The joint statement was read out by the Russian delegation at the IAEA Board of Governors’ meeting in Vienna on Wednesday, under the agenda item on the implementation of Iran’s Safeguards Agreement.
​
The three countries said that military attacks and threats against Iran and its safeguarded nuclear facilities violate the United Nations Charter and undermine the conditions necessary for the IAEA to carry out its verification activities.
​
They stressed that continued military threats and the consequences of attacks on nuclear facilities have made the normal implementation of safeguards measures practically impossible, adding that these circumstances must be taken into account in any assessment of the agency’s activities in Iran.
​
Iran, China and Russia also rejected unconditional demands for the normal implementation of safeguards measures at damaged nuclear facilities without addressing the obstacles caused by military aggression and continued threats.
​
The statement further noted that Iran has authorized all planned IAEA inspections at the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant in 2026, demonstrating its continued commitment to safeguards obligations and cooperation with the agency despite the difficult circumstances.
​
The three countries described political and diplomatic engagement and dialogue based on mutual respect as the only practical way forward, calling on all relevant parties to take constructive steps to facilitate cooperation between Tehran and the IAEA.
